notes.title: WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes - Important Update
notes.content:
Hello,

We’d like to share some important information about the upcoming changes in WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes.

As per our previous announcement, players who owned WARSAW in their libraries prior to August 23, 2023, will receive an update with a special launcher on May 20, 2024. This launcher allows those players to choose between playing WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes or the older version of the game, which was previously available on the “bootcamp” beta branch. At the same time, both available beta branches of WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes will be closed. This change affects the 'legacy_version' branch, which contains the older version of the game, and the 'bootcamp' branch, which was used for public testing for updates. 

Achievements and save files:
[list]
[*] Achievements on Steam are tied to the current version of WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes and not the older version of the game. Completing the campaign in the current version of WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes will be required to unlock all the achievements. 
[*] Save files from the 'legacy_version' branch will remain compatible with the older version of the game with one exception - if you saved the game during the tutorial, you will have to start over due to the changes introduced in the meantime. [/list]
Players who never purchased the previous version before the launch of WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes will continue to have access to the current version only. That means if you added WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes to your library after August 23, 2023, and started your playthrough of the older version of the game from either “bootcamp” or “legacy_branch”, you have until May 20, 2024 to complete it.

WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes Team

notes.title: WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes - Upcoming changes
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Thank you for all the feedback you’ve been sharing with us since the release of WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes. We’d like to use this opportunity to let you know what the next steps are and at the same time answer some of the most frequent questions that arose on Steam after WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes launched.  

On August 23, 2023 WARSAW was updated to WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes and became available on Steam as a free game featuring: 
[list]
[*] New playable hero
[*] Two new enemy units
[*] New storyline, complete with animated and voiced cutscenes
[*] New, fully voiced Polish narrator (with complete subtitles)
[*] New soundtrack
[*] New location type to interact with on the map
[*] Tons of new entries for the codex including photos, posters and newspapers
[/list]
Alongside there have been two beta branches with older versions of the game available to all the players. That beta has run its course and will close in 30 days. On April 5th, 2024, we will retire all the beta branches from WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes. Players who had the game in their library before August 23, 2023, will receive an update that adds a special launcher. This launcher will allow you to choose which version of the game you want to play - WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes or the older version of the game (with improved controller support, optimization, balance updates, bug fixes, and other quality-of-life changes).

Those of you who did not purchase the previous version of the game and did not have it in their library prior to the WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes launch will retain access to that version only.  

[b]Q: Why did you remove a strategic element from the game, making the gameplay too linear?[/b]
A: The removal of the “momentum” system was required to follow for historical accuracy - this means that Rising cannot falter based on the player’s choices that are not true to the historical facts. Currently the linear mission progression requires the player to undertake a mix of both the actual missions that happened in real life, as well as a degree of random missions to make each gameplay that much different but it does not affect the historical milestones of the actual Rising.
The second thing altered was the omission of three missions to choose from - what now remains is a random mission that propels the story forward in linear fashion, although the random missions are still chosen from a pool of available ones.	

WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes remains a tactical turn-based RPG with a wide roster of playable characters with their own unique skills, that tells the story of Warsaw Rising - now presented in more accurate chronological order. When playing the game you will experience:
[list]
[*] Tactical turn-based gameplay with rpg elements and resource management
[*] Extensive roster of characters with their own unique skills
[*] Collection of weapons that players can find on different missions
[*] Numerous enemies and enemy vehicles with their own sets of skills and strategies
[*] The events of the Warsaw Rising accompanied by historical characters, places and documents
[/list]
[b]Q: Game became a visual novel now.[/b]
A: WARSAW RISING’S gameplay remains the same as in the older version and now players also have the opportunity to learn more about the events, people, and places of the Warsaw Rising. WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes is a turn-based rpg that has an extensive, tactical combat system where players can develop their characters that have their own playstyle, weapons and story. It portrays the events of the 1944 Warsaw Rising, one of the most tragic chapters in the city’s long history.

[b]Q: Game is not historically accurate.[/b]
A: We partnered with Institute of Polish Remembrance to expand on the historical aspect of the game, to enrich WARSAW RISING with the addition of authentic events, characters, missions, cutscenes and Warsaw Rising day by day diary. Warsaw Rising Museum and Institute of Polish Remembrance supplied us with the materials that contributed to the historical accuracy of the game - photos of people and places, notes, and newspaper clippings.

[b]Q: I lost access to the game that I paid for. How do I get it back?[/b]
A: Access to the older version of the game was never removed - it required you to access the beta branch to play it. Starting from April 5th 2024 we will introduce a launcher that allows owners of the older version of the game to choose which version they want to play.

We greatly appreciate your support, comments and feedback for WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes.

[i][b]UPDATE:[/b]

We decided to postpone the beta branch deactivation by two weeks into the second half of April.[/i]

notes.title: Accessing the Legacy Version
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Yesterday’s launch of the new Free version of WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes was a technically challenging affair. Switching the game live, from one version to another, with a major overhaul of the features and content, Steam page assets, the name of the game and the price tag was not without its challenges and we had all hands on board for this. 

It was never our intention to remove the access to the original version of the game. Unfortunately due to the technical challenges outlined above we ran out of time yesterday and didn’t make it available for the launch of WARSAW RISING. Sorry!

As a result we’ve prepared a Legacy Version branch where everyone can access WARSAW as it was before August 23rd and experience the original version of the game.

In order to access the Legacy Branch of the game please select WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes in your Steam Library, right click on the title, select “Properties” and then “BETAS” tab. Choose “Legacy Version” which should automatically update to the version of the game from before August 23rd.  
Moreover, we will continue to iron out the bugs and hotfix both the WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes version of the game, as well as the Legacy Version. Our aim is to introduce the existing Bootcamp Branch changes (controller support, patches, etc) into the Legacy Version after extensive testing in the near future. Please note that the Bootcamp improvements are already available in the WARSAW RISING version of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/1b3c44a98978f364cd23a760bd6261ac6a669084.png[/img]

Thank you for your patience and understanding while we were working out the best way to move forward after yesterday’s launch. We want to make sure that you can enjoy both WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes and have a chance to come back to the Legacy Version, if you feel like it.      
WARSAW RISING focuses more on the historical accuracy when compared to the 2019 original. It was important to get the events, places and people right. For this to work, we had to adjust the strategic layer of the game. We achieved this by removing the "momentum" system and the random mission generation, because they allowed for unpredictable and unhistorical progress of the uprising (ie. Śródmieście falling in the opening days of the struggle). The game now follows a more linear but also a more authentic timeline.

The rest of the strategic layer, however, remains intact. Random calendar events, hero recruitment, inventory, character progression, hospital are all still in the game. In addition to historical missions, the game will present you with randomly generated ones, similar to the 2019 original. This way the campaign retains replayable elements instead of being fully "on rails"

New features of WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes

-        New playable hero
-        Two new enemy units
-        New storyline, complete with animated and voiced cutscenes
-        New, authentic Polish narrator (with complete subtitles)
-        New soundtrack
-        New location type to interact with on the map
-        Tons of new entries for the codex including photos, posters and newspapers
-        Console improvements (Bootcamp branch) are now available in the PC version, including controller support
-        UI, visuals and gameplay improvements
-        Huge performance improvements for the city map

Thank you for your support and understanding

WARSAW RISING: City of Heroes Team

notes.title: Development Update: November 2021
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Welcome to another Development Update on the changes we are implementing for Warsaw: Homecoming.

[b]Before we begin, [url=https://discord.gg/N8CCVNkCkj]please consider joining our official Discord channel[/url][/b], which has a shiny brand-new section dedicated to Warsaw. If you feel an urge to discuss (or contest!) any of the following design choices directly with us devs, then you can do so there.

Now, today we're going to be taking an in-depth look at some of the changes planned for our [b]battle system[/b]. As we have previously discussed [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1026420/announcements/detail/2867095129587274611]last month[/url] the plan is to significantly up the tempo, remove the awkward pauses, increase lethality, and streamline some of the mechanics. Let's see how we're proposing to do that:

Changes TL:DR;
[list]
[*] New lane system with a single, long lane
[*] New cover system (with heavy and light variants)
[*] New activation system with individual action points
[*] New range system
[*] Streamlined ammunition
[*] Revamped UI
[/list]

So, firstly, [b]we are removing the two lane (4x2) system from the game.[/b] We anticipate that this decision might prove controversial for some of you, but we strongly believe that this is the correct way forward. When we started creating Warsaw we had two possible plans in mind: either a single lane, or a 3x3 grid. The 4x2 arrangement we ended up with was a bad compromise, and while it has some benefits, it also brings a lot of problems.

The new single lane will be 6 spots wide on each side, and it will not collapse in on itself when there is an empty spot available. This will allow us to retain tactical movement (such as that which we had in the original game) while also introducing big improvements. It will allow us to create a better combatant UI, more intuitive skill ranges, and generally a better visual arrangement of elements on the screen.

[b]Cover will work in a different way[/b] in Homecoming. The barricades will now become a part of a cell (or a cell modifier, if you will), rather than taking up their own place. They will be split into two categories: heavy and light, each with distinct bonuses. In addition, the penalty of getting shot while out of cover will be much harsher, increasing the importance of keeping your head low.

[b]Activation points are now individual instead of being shared[/b]. Each character will be able to store up to 3 AP, and will regenerate 2 AP each round. Actions mostly cost 1 AP, which means you'll be able to perform more than one action in an activation. However, some (usually destructive) skills or manoeuvres can cost more... leading to some interesting choices. 

[b]The range system has been completely revamped.[/b] Range will be relative to the position the character is standing in. For example, you may have a pistol skill with range 1, which can only be used from the first spot. Meanwhile, a weapon with range 2 can hit up to two spaces forward, so you can either shoot at the second enemy from the first spot, or shoot at the first enemy from the second spot (and so on). All of the usual features (like area of effect and minimal ranges) remain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/e3f0397ca8b8151bb0207bfac3fc6c99dbf7360e.jpg[/img]

[b]Ammunition is being streamlined into a single, unified resource.[/b] Ultimately, we decided that the split into three types didn't produce anything meaningful enough to justify its inclusion, and the same effect can be achieved by scaling the amount of ammo you have to use accordingly. The new system will be more readable and easier to understand. Less inventory mess too!

[b]Finally, we will be completely reorganising the UI.[/b] Important character information such as health, AP, debuffs, etc, will be now displayed next to the character. This will allow for a little more breathing space at the sides of the screen, and the challenges will be integrated at the top instead of sitting awkwardly in the middle. We are also looking at improving the bottom section of the battle UI thanks to the new ammunition system, but we are not ready to share any of the visuals yet.

Well, that's it for this month, folks! We very much look forward to hearing your feedback on the proposed changes. Let us know what you think, either in the comments here, or on our Discord!

notes.title: Development Update: October 2021
notes.content:
Hey guys,

As you are probably aware we have announced a new, refreshed version of [i]Warsaw[/i] called [i]Warsaw: Homecoming[/i], which is currently in development. Starting today, we will be posting monthly [b]Development Updates[/b] detailing project progress and giving you a peek behind the curtain.

Before we get started, allow me to introduce myself. My name is Bartek. I am one of the owners at Pixelated Milk, and the guy who oversees projects at the studio. You are likely familiar with me, since I am the person who usually writes these posts and answers on the forums (@barjed), but I'd like to introduce myself anyway. Fresh start and all that. 

Now, let's dive in!

[h1]The Goal[/h1]

There's no escaping the fact that Warsaw had issues at launch. Some of those issues were addressed in patches, but many still remain. [b]Our goal with [i]Homecoming[/i] is therefore to completely overhaul the game[/b]. We'll be adding new features, improving the old ones, and even including some new assets! Our hope is that the new product will satisfy the veterans of the game and also attract new fans. Please also remember that [i]Warsaw: Homecoming[/i] will be free to the existing owners of [i]Warsaw[/i].

[b]TL:DR;[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/10236e8b121577cc959231d3649aa24745cf869e.png[/img]

[h2]Improvements: Battle System[/h2]

Three main issues we will be addressing in the Battle System are [b]battle pacing[/b], [b]skill ranges[/b] and [b]ammunition[/b].

Right now the battles feel way too slow and you often end up with a single enemy who cannot easily be targeted, which is very frustrating. [b]Damage and health calculations will be re-calibrated across the board[/b]. Lethality will also increase, and with it, the general pacing of the battles will also improve.

[b]The character positioning system will be upgraded dramatically[/b]. We want to preserve the tactical nature of character placement, but also feel the current iteration is needlessly confusing (two lanes) and leads to un-intuitive situations. 

Finally, [b]the importance of ammunition will be increased[/b]. We want to streamline the management of individual bullets, while retaining the signature feel of being low on expensive ammunition. This will also result in expensive skills feeling more impactful and powerful.

[h2]Improvements: The Narrative[/h2]

A completely new storyline is coming to Warsaw, which will tie all of the existing content together in a neat and emotional narrative. Currently-limited stories and character arcs will be expanded, the events of the Uprising will be explained in greater detail, and the whole experience should be greatly improved. 

The presentation of the story will also be refreshed with a brand new interface that will unify both the existing emergent events and the new critical path storyline.

[h2]Improvements: The Strategy Layer[/h2]

While clearly inspired by XCOM, the strategy layer fell short in Warsaw, and will be reworked. Following feedback, the current "calendar" will be dropped completely (it was clunky and not very intuitive). Instead, we will mesh this layer with the newly added narrative. Your decisions will be tied with the historically unfolding events of the Uprising, and should be much more hard-hitting this time around. They will lead to branching outcomes. For example, by electing to aid a particular section of the Uprising, you will unlock a new character... at the cost of losing someone else.

[h2]Improvements: The Exploration[/h2]

Without disrupting the general flow of the exploration sections of [i]Warsaw[/i], we feel we can improve them significantly to enhance gameplay.

[b]Enemies will be much more threatening[/b]. They will gain the ability to move instead of just passively sitting there.

[b]RNG will be dropped for Mission generation[/b]. Instead we will prepare a selection of handmade, high-quality missions with better placement for interesting objectives, secrets, and more. 

[b]New points of interest will be added to the maps[/b]. 

[h2]Improvements: Theme[/h2]

There is a lot of historical accuracy in Warsaw already. Authentic weapon types (including some rare ones like Błyskawica), characters based on reality (such as the Berling's Soldier), events dealing with historic occurences (Pasta's destruction, etc). The theme grows weaker in some parts of the game however - such as in the gameplay itself.

For this reason, [b]we want to align the theme of the game more closely with the gameplay[/b]. You will see an Uprising even more similar to that of reality, with insurgents getting pushed back to the Śródmieście, and missions less about attacking and more about defending against the superior German forces. 

[h2]Improvements: Soundtrack[/h2]

One area we've focused on especially for improvement is the game's soundtrack. Our plan is to provide [b]a new, immersive soundtrack for Homecoming[/b] of greater quality (and quantity). It will also be a great tool to illustrate the shifting tides and emotions of the new storyline of the game.

[h2]Improvements: A Shedload of Other New Stuff[/h2]

As you can see, [i]Homecoming[/i] focuses mostly on the fundamentals of the game, and that's our priority. However, we do want to expand the rest of the game too. You can expect [b]new enemy types[/b] and [b]items[/b] in addition to everything listed before.

-

So, that's all for today! Over the upcoming months we will discuss the individual sections outlined today in far greater detail. We are excited to see how we can improve the game, and we hope you will join us on this journey.

See you next month!

notes.title: WARSAW - new tutorial, new controllers support, new improvements
notes.content:
The year is coming to an end and we wanted to share the newest update with you today. 

While working on the console versions of [b]WARSAW[/b] (available on Switch, Xbox One, PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5, and Xbox series S and X as well) we decided we will want to touch upon and improve certain areas of the game. And these are now – courtesy of the backport - hitting your PC’s today. To make sure this is not something that we are forcing down your throats we will include this as a beta branch of the game where you will be able to feedback the content and take it for a spin before this is rolled into a patch for everyone. To touch upon all the new features incorporated into [b]WARSAW[/b] please find the list below: 

-	Reworked tutorial – which should offer a better introduction to the game for those who hadn’t had the chance to pick it up yet. And for those who had, all the stuff we have added post-launch will now be a part of the tutorial as well 
-	Full control support – with native glyphs for all the already not so next gen controllers for PS4, Xbox and Switch
-	Optimization – a lot of the stuff has been rewritten with performance in mind. Any stutters or lag you had encountered should now be adjusted
-	Quality of life changes – major of which is the opportunity to change the party formation during city traversal
-	UI improvements for a better UX 
-	Bug fixes and balance changes – including achievement fixes and addressing the save file problem encountered when the game is closed during saving             

The build will be firstly available on the beta branch – here’s how to access it: 

1. For starters, you must have [b]WARSAW[/b] added to your Steam library.
2. Right click on [b]WARSAW[/b] on the library list and open Properties.
3. Click on the BETA tab, go to beta Dropdown list and choose the “bootcamp” branch.
4. No password is required so Steam should start downloading the game automatically.
5. Play the game!

Please let us know what you think in the comments on the forum.

notes.title: "Żmija" part 2 - Bootcamp
notes.content:
Ding, ding, ding!

The progression update is here!

Because this is such a big change to how the underlying systems of the game work, we've made a new Feedback topic for these changes exclusively. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/1026420/discussions/0/1752399266008348077/]You can find it here[/url]. Please let us know if things now feel better, worse, easier, harder or anything else you can think of! 

We'll be tweaking the balance of the new XP systems in the upcoming days, before the patch goes to the public branch to make sure it's balanced well.

So here's what you get in this patch.

[h1]Experience Points[/h1][list]
[*] Your characters now gain XP by completing certain tasks in the game, like fighting enemies or completing Missions.
[*] XP can be spent on acquiring new Skills and Perks.
[*] Characters no longer have to follow a randomized progression tree. All Skills are available for purchase from the get go.
[*] XP is unique per character. [i]That's a nice, powerful Franek you have there. Shame if something would happen to him...[/i]
[*] Commendations can be used to grant additional XP points to any character you want, even ones that did not participate in a given mission.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/e3d436ea57feabdeedf70326fcc9a8f27299261d.png[/img]

[h1]Challenges[/h1][list]
[*] Two optional challenges are now generated in each battle you fight
[*] These are small objectives like achieving victory without moving, avoiding a certain type of ammunition, prevailing in a set number of turns, etc.
[*] Completing these optional challenges will net you additional XP for all participating characters
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/cbf347b4ba12af17dfe19e9960345477ad4f95ee.png[/img]

[h1]Perks[/h1][list]
[*] Characters can now buy Perks by spending XP in addition to Skills
[*] Perks confer passive bonuses to attributes, like Accuracy, Health, Resilience, etc.
[*] There are over 20 perks available to buy for each character
[/list]

In additional to all that we have also fixed the bug with Steam achievements popping up only after the game is closed.

Enjoy and let us know what you think!

notes.title: "ŻMIJA" PREVIEW
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

New stuff is coming to Warsaw later this month as discussed in the previous update. Let's take a look at how all of those changes will impact both the character progression and the codex.

[h3]CODEX [/h3]

"Żmija" will bring a significantly improved codex experience to you all.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/c03934d54d6a5fe62952ebfcf4319f1934447dfc.png[/img]

[list]
[*]UI was completely redone in order to make it more consistent with the rest of the game. The previous iteration had a very tiny text box with large fonts, which made reading stuff a chore. For the new version the "front page" was removed and integrated with the entry list to reduce the amount of clicks necessary to access an entry. 

[*] Locked parts of an entry (mainly in the characters' backstories) are now clearly marked with a grey color. Entry parts are also now separated for additional readability.

[*] You have asked for the epilogues to display in the codex and we have listened. Unlocked epilogues are now permanently added to a characters' codex entry.

[*] We now display skills of characters, weapons and ENEMIES (!) in the codex. You can check tooltips of German abilities to better prepare for what lies ahead.

[*] Attributes (health, accuracy, resistances, etc.) of characters and enemies are now displayed in the codex.

[*] Finally, the codex can be accessed from any part of the game, including from the battle!

[/list]

[h3]CHARACTER PROGRESSION [/h3]

This is another total makeover of an important system that will be a part of the "Żmija" update. 

[list]
[*] Characters now gain experience (XP) for winning fights, completing missions and so on.

[*] XP is gained per character. Benched characters do not gain XP.

[*] Additional XP can be gained by awarding medals to characters. This way your old medals will be still useful in the new system and you will also have a way to boost your reserve insurgents.

[*] Old characters levels (Rookie, Veteran, etc.) are gone!

[*] Randomized character skill trees are gone!

[*] Instead all Skills now have a XP cost added to them. A character can "buy" any skill at any time as long as he or she has XP to pay for it. 

[*] New feature is added to the game - Perks!

[*] Perks are passive attribute bonuses, which increase health, accuracy, resistances, etc. A number of perks are available in the game. Perks are "bought" using XP, just like skills. After a perk is bought, it is automatically applied to a character from now on. More ways to customize your guys and gals!

[*] Another new feature is added to the game - Battle Challenges!

[*] Each battle in the game now has two optional challenges that you can complete for additional XP. These range from limiting yourself to a particular type of ammo, not moving, etc. Challenges should result in more varied battles and provide a more rewarding experience with their risk/reward scenarios.  
[/list]

We have also fixed a number of bugs reported by you on our forums and did additional balance passes to various element of the game. 

See you in "Żmija" later this month!

notes.title: CONTENT UPDATE "RADOSŁAW" Part 1 - Bootcamp Branch
notes.content:
Heya folks,

we're still hard at work tinkering with the "Radosław" larger changes so we've decided to post a first part of the update today.

If you enjoyed our work over the last few weeks and the updates, perhaps consider changing your Steam Review? It would be a massive help!

So here we go, "Radosław" part 1

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/8ff37d3a86e48b73af148452fc6f960d6e29e48d.png[/img]

[h1]CONTENT[/h1]
[u]NEW BOSS - Sturmpanzer IV Brummbär[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/915893277229dfef12a582df58b49cdb0bc0f8ff.png[/img]

A new type of a German tank takes to the field. Brummbär is a more resilient, more deadly variation of the Panzer IV. With over 90% damage reduction and a devastating main cannon this one will be a challenge for the insurgents. 

This enemy also comes with it's own, new mission type you can embark on from the Hideout.

[h1]QUALITY OF LIFE[/h1]
- Selling value of items is now displayed in their tooltips

[h1]BALANCE[/h1]
- Decreased aoe range of Cocktail Party
- Increased aoe range of Incite
- Reduced Stamina cost of Interference

[h1]BUG FIXES[/h1]
- Fixed Kill Squad working incorrectly
- Fixed Stand By incorrectly triggering reactions
- General fixes for the Executioner's starting skills
- Fixed loading screen displaying incorrectly in some cases
- Fixed broken Revenge description in languages other than English
- Fixed game language getting "stuck" to English in some windows
- Fixed Ambush description in languages other than English
- Fixed broken difficulty descriptions in languages other than English
- Fixed broken strings when looting in languages other then English

[h1]OTHER[/h1]
- Added 'settings' file (with unlocks) to the Steam Cloud Sync

notes.title: NEW ROADMAP
notes.content:
Heya folks,

we're back with the promised new Roadmap for the rest of this year. Exciting [b]FREE [/b] changes are coming to Warsaw - all based on your feedback!

[h1]NEW ROADMAP[/h1]
New free content!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/dc9dba0b016f9ee808e2b03453bec345de84373d.png[/img]

[u]NOVEMBER - UPDATE "RADOSŁAW"[/u]

[b]+ NEW CONTENT - Heavy German Reinforcements - a new Boss [/b]

[b]+ NEW FEATURE - Combat Objectives[/b]

Complete optional Battle Objectives for additional rewards! Each battle gets a fresh set of objectives for a completely different experience and increased variety. In the future Battle Objectives will seamlessly merge with the upcoming Character Progression Overhaul, forming a deeper, more engaging system.

[b]+ NEW FEATURE - Codex Overhaul[/b]

Total refresh of the way the Codex is presented. Check all unlocked things at a glance and easily track enemies, weapons, and characters that you have not met yet. Check the skills and stats of weapons and enemies. Read all the characters epilogues you have already seen and even check the requirements of the elusive personal missions!

[u]DECEMBER - UPDATE "ŻMIJA"[/u]

[b]+ NEW FEATURE - Character Progression Overhaul[/b]

Out with the old, in with the new. Characters now earn Experience Points for their achievements which can be used to acquire new skills and perks. XP is earned through Missions, Combat Objectives, Narrative Events, and more. Perks are added to the progression tree which let you choose passive attribute bonuses for your characters. Skills in the progression tree are no longer random and now allow for more choices and player agency. 

Both updates will add more bug fixes, quality of life features and other polishing stuff. 

Additional goodies are also planned for the near future!

notes.title: CONTENT UPDATE "ŻNIWIARZ" - NOW LIVE!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/4b61db93170594ea65c9d3038747bd67e01a8dc1.png[/img]

Another large update lands on the public branch today - Żniwiarz! It brings a lot of new stuff plus the anticipated Melee feature to the game.

[h1]CONTENT[/h1]
[u]NEW FEATURE - MELEE[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/7c0724c78274d7b44aef84a0d3696c92dbf168ce.png[/img]

Every character has gained a new skill in their repertoire - a melee attack! These can be used from any place and may target any enemy on the grid. No ammo needed! The kicker here is that these melee attacks are not very powerful; still, they can be quite useful in a pinch.

And wait, there's more! Multiple melee attack types are now available in the game. Some characters simply deal damage while others also push or pull the enemies for some additional utility!

[u]NEW FEATURE - EASY MODE[/u]

You asked for it and we delivered. A fourth difficulty, "Easy", is available now for the more casual players who want a more relaxed challenge level in the game.

[u]NEW CHARACTER - ERNEST BUDNIK THE EXECUTIONER[/u]

Within the ranks of the Home Army, there are men and women tasked with carrying out death sentences issued by the Polish Underground State. When justice falls short, they act. Ernest is one such executioner.

Ernest wields revolvers and machine guns. He also has a whole arsenal of unique skills. First and foremost, he's able to apply Awareness to any ally which lets them target any position on the enemy grid while attacking. He's no slouch in other areas, though: Guillotine turns his revolver shots into Critical Hits, On the Mark ignores any Accuracy or Dodge modifiers of the enemy while using machine guns, and to round it all off, he has the ability to heal himself upon killing an enemy. Lots of interesting tactical options!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/1be36ddd1455924fbaa6926e528c44d6c3b944cb.png[/img]

[u]NEW NARRATIVE EVENT - "The Verdict"[/u]

Ernest's personal event in which a shadow is cast upon the figure of the executioner.

[u]NEW CODEX ENTRIES AND A NEW EPILOGUE[/u]

Both for the new character.

[u]NEW WEAPONS - MG13 & PANZERFAUST[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/f88143cd4d765fdc99471770b5200e40a8866748.png[/img]

[h1]BUG FIXING[/h1]
- Fixed multiple issues with usable consumables.
- Fixed Wurfgerät being moved incorrectly.
- Fixed Jan's portrait in the epilogue.
- Fixed Grim Bravery (again!).
- Fixed Soothing Presence.
- Fixed Cap Off.
- Fixed Survivor.
- Fixed some broken and missing audio in skills.
- Fixed missing localization strings.
- Fixed Codex and context menu UI displaying incorrectly in some cases.
- Fixed Inventory UI in the Hideout while multiple items are present.

[h1]QUALITY OF LIFE[/h1]
- Slight tweaks to the battle UI.
- Simplified 3D models of the destroyed city for shorter loading times.

[h1]WHAT'S NEXT?[/h1]
With "Żniwiarz" deployed, we have reached the end of our roadmap for October. Now is the time to look back and reevaluate the collected feedback and prepare a new November roadmap for you all, We'll share it with you when it's ready. Don't worry, though, it won't be long. 

Here's a small teaser though - a COMPLETE revamp of character progression is coming!

notes.title: CONTENT UPDATE "ZOŚKA" - NOW LIVE!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/ace278d6e5125f5b81416aad031c00f83835e68e.png[/img]

[h1]CONTENT[/h1]
[u]NEW FEATURE - STEALTH[/u]

Use a new consumable item, "Camouflage", to become invisible when exploring the city. Avoid German patrols and their line of sight zones. 

[u]NEW FEATURE - AMBUSH[/u]

Turn the tables on your enemies! Approach the Germans while in stealth to ambush them and gain advantage in battle. Ambushed enemies have their initial amount of Activations reduced by 1.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/4707b117f63e9440238c5a5564b4d31dc068fb9f.png[/img]

[u]NEW ENEMY - SS Veteran[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/feb7aad9c38641466f6e59d6fd16e96fa13472e2.png[/img]

Armed with a deadly Panzerfaust, this veteran enemy can deplete the Stamina of your Insurgents, destroy barricades, and unleash a hail of bullets with his looted PPSH.

[u]NEW ENEMY - Wurfgerät 42[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/276601717b54d1e853df230fa22eae88daf7fe83.png[/img]

Technically part of the Nebelwerfer family, the Wurfgerät 42 is a unique type of enemy consisting of two separate elements: the weapon and the operator. Killing the operator early prevents the launcher from firing, but if you wait too long, the Wurfgerät 42 will rain fire upon your team for devastating AOE damage.

[u]NEW NARRATIVE EVENT - "Step by Step"[/u]

Surrounded and left with no options, a family attempts a daring escape.

[h1]QUALITY OF LIFE[/h1]
- Persistent consumable items like the Compass or the new Camouflage now display a nifty icon, which clearly shows the remaining time before they expire.

Plus multiple minor bug fixes.

[h1]BALANCE[/h1]
- Increased critical chance of Make Way
- Increased range and damage of Guardian Angel and reduced its ammo cost
- Increased Bleed chance of Hack
- Increased Bleed chance of Blade Rush
- Increased range of Foray
- Increased damage of Root Out and reduced its ammo cost
- Increased accuracy, range and critical chance of Showdown and reduced its ammo cost
- Increased range of Enmity
- Increased range of Reckoning and reduced its ammo cost
- Reduced ammo cost of Nemesis
- Adjusted Will to live
- Increased range of Signal Corruption
- Reduced range of Fake Transmission
- Increased range of Single Out
- Increased Blind chance of Fake Transmission

notes.title: CONTENT UPDATE "PARASOL" - NOW LIVE!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/3f84f927ab323ca4f2b93f9cf79e1c269f14427d.png[/img]

[h1]CONTENT[/h1]
[u]NEW PLAYABLE CHARACTER - JAN CIEŚLAK THE WATCHMAN[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/6e355a4d505f91280ebe640bd628ce455e82291c.png[/img]

Jan is a member of the famous 1107th Home Army platoon which consisted in large part of deaf and mute resistance fighters. He wields rifles and grenades.

His combat efficiency depends on the positioning of the enemy. As such, comboing him with characters who are able to reposition the Germans will be of great help. In addition, he can increase the activation costs of the enemy to 2 points instead of the usual 1. The nature of his condition also grants him increased resistance to Suppression.

On the flip side, due to his inability to communicate through speech, he cannot pass any narrative event checks that rely on Charm, Academics, or Intuition.

[u]NEW FEATURE - TURBO MODE[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/ac8219867b5b352ec286b2719559b69cd17513eb.png[/img]

You can now adjust the animation speed during battles. Increase it to 1.5x, or even 2x, and enjoy a more snappy gameplay. The game will also remember your last selected speed and apply it every time you get into a fight.

[u]NEW NARRATIVE EVENT - "Inaudible"[/u]

Jan's personal narrative event in which we learn that pain and grief transcend words.

[u]NEW CODEX ENTRIES AND A NEW EPILOGUE[/u]

Both for the new character.

[u]NEW WEAPON - Mannlicher 1888[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/6aab9e255b596bc1c3588f4668111a6eb925613f.png[/img]

[u]NEW WEAPON - Steyr 1912[/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/6f3ce01aadb1c9b9cf7b68a41b930194b257e892.png[/img]

[h1]QUALITY OF LIFE[/h1]
- You can now move a single item instead of the whole stack in the preparation screen. Hold Left Shift when clicking on an item to trigger this.

[h1]BUG FIXES[/h1]
- Skill tooltips are now correctly updated after a weapon is swapped in the hideout.
- Fixed the starting skills of the Uhlan and the Phone Operator.
- Fixed SS Officers' portraits.

notes.title: CONTENT UPDATE "BASZTA" - NOW LIVE!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/a1495d620ffacb26096a9035d99863fddd51b127.png[/img]

[url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suppression_of_Mokot%C3%B3w]"Baszta"[/url] is upon us! 

[u]"BASZTA" IS NOW LIVE FOR EVERYONE ON THE PUBLIC BRANCH![/u] 

[h1]CONTENT[/h1]
[u]NEW FEATURE - DIFFICULTY LEVELS[/u]

We're proud to present you this anticipated feature a week early! Starting a new campaign will let you choose between three difficulty levels for both the battles and the strategic map.

Regular difficulty level is the one you've been playing so far. Challenging difficulty level is similar but slightly easier than the one the game launched with. Extreme difficulty level is for the most confident veterans!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/9f87967c5e34a8ae80baa1ceac837ac4e2d522ff.png[/img]

[u]NEW FEATURE - STARTING PARTY CUSTOMIZATION[/u]

You can now select your starting characters when you launch a new non-tutorial campaign. Unlock new characters to select from by recruiting them in your previous campaigns! 

[u]NEW FEATURE - VOLUNTEER CUSTOMIZATION[/u]

You can now freely select both the weapon and the support skills when recruiting a new Volunteer. Say goodbye to the RNG! It's also possible to go with random values if that is your wish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/b876da357f875be0056e569d4dbae9bafe0453b3.png[/img]

[u]NEW FEATURE - SKIPPING TIME IN THE HIDEOUT[/u]

Lots of wounded characters? Waiting for that 'New Blood' event? You can now skip the time in the Hideout without embarking on a new mission. Giving your team a breather is priceless but watch out because waiting in the comfort of the Hideout means all three available mission on that day will count as failed!

[u]NEW NARRATIVE EVENT - "A Discourse in Ballistics"[/u]

Everyone likes cannons. But do you know how to operate them?

[u]NEW ENEMY - SAPPER[/u]

Do you like to hide your characters behind cover? The Sapper can destroy player barricades with a single skill, deploy cover on the German side and make a deadly salvo with his MP40.

[u]NEW ENEMY - JAEGER[/u]

Deadly and effective, the Jaeger will move to benefit from any cover available on the map while buffing himself at the same time. He is also armed with his trusty G43 and will make short work of your characters if you leave them in the open.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/d2f546d79de895ce93415322ee7986f066ad07e2.png[/img]

[h1]BALANCE[/h1]
- Significantly increased the chance of recruitment for the Ex-Prisoner, the Uhlan and the Radiooperator. Most of you haven't seen them even once so here's a shot in the arm!

[h1]QUALITY OF LIFE[/h1]
- Refreshed the Commander interface in the Hideout. Active missions and excursions are now displayed on the minimap. Excursions have received a face-lifting to make them more pleasing to the eye and to also make them consistent with the rest of the game.

[h1]BUG FIXES[/h1]
- In an effort to prevent save data corruption in rare cases, the codex will now save itself less frequently
- (Hotfix #3) Fixed battles freezing in rare cases, mostly due to reactive skills
- Increased text duration in the epilogues for easier reading
- Fixed the Chemical Mishap skill
- Fixed a bug when the game would fail to launch due to a video player missing in the OS - Windows Enterprise and N versions mainly

notes.title: OCTOBER CONTENT ROADMAP
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

The first patch has landed so it's time for the promised October Content Roadmap for Warsaw. The whole team is pumped up to fix the lingering issues, add new content and new features.

We are happy to announce that starting tomorrow we are bringing you a large content update [b][u]EVERY WEEK[/u][/b]!

These also add frequently requested features like an option to attack without ammo (stab with the bayonet!), difficulty levels, passing time when in the Hideout, expanded Side Missions, new strategic options, customizable Volunteers and much, much more!

Take a look!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34601314/917ee78536d4127f378df2a2887e9b9903a4d0a4.png[/img]

Here it is in the glorious text form:

[b]4.10.2019 UPDATE "RUCZAJ"[/b]
- New battle location
- New narrative event

[b]10.10.2019 UPDATE "BASZTA"[/b]
- German Reinforcements - 2 new Enemies
- New narrative event
- New feature - passing time in hideout. Wait for a good opportunity before embarking on a mission!
- New feature - customizable Volunteers. Choose a load-out for your new Volunteer instead of relying on the RNG!

[b]17.10.2019 UPDATE "PARASOL"[/b]
- Polish Reinforcements - 1 new playable Insurgent
- New narrative event
- 2 new weapons
- New feature - Difficulty levels. Adjust the challenge level of the game to your preference. Tweak combat and strategic difficulty separately!

[b]24.10.2019 UPDATE "ZOŚKA"[/b]
- German Reinforcements - 2 new Enemies
- New narrative event
- New feature - Stealth. Avoid and ambush your enemies for additional advantages in combat!

[b]31.10.2019 UPDATE "ŻNIWIARZ"[/b]
- Polish Reinforcements - 1 new playable Insurgent
- New narrative event
- 2 new weapons
- New feature - Melee. No ammo? No problem! Fight the Nazis with fists, stocks and bayonets!
- Improved feature - Better Side Missions. Recover Attrition, prevent Morale loss, find loot and send your Insurgents on Excursions!

All five updates are named after military units which took part in the Uprising (for example [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%BBniwiarz_Group]Żniwiarz Group[/url]).

Thank you for sticking with us. The best is yet to come!

notes.title: FIRST PATCH INCOMING
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We are listening to your feedback and are committed to improving Warsaw both in short and long term. We aim to provide you a content roadmap in the very near future. 

A patch will be deployed shortly, which addresses a number of issues you have asked about since launch.

[b]DELETING SAVE FILES[/b]

Deleting saves from the game now works correctly.

[b]DIFFICULTY ADJUSTMENT[/b]

While we want the game to remain difficult it seems clear from the feedback that it was over-tuned. We have reduced the overall difficulty across the board.

- Health of Enemies reduced by 10%. This will also speed up the combat
- Reduced the maximum number of Enemies in battles from 7 to 6
- Ammunition cost of all Skills reduced by 20%
- Decreased the rate of AP consumption when moving around the city by 25%.
- Reduced the rate of Momentum decay by 10%
- Increased the starting amount of Short Ammunition by 10%
- Increased the starting amount of Long Ammunition by 25%
- Increased the starting amount of Heavy Ammunition by 50%
- Slightly increased ammunition gain from looting

[b]RNG ADJUSTMENT[/b]

Right now the game increases your hit odds by 10% when you miss. We have increased this to 30%. This should reduce the amount of frustrating missing streaks in combat.

[b]BUG FIXES[/b]

- Fixed a rare bug where battles failed to load
- Fixed tooltips in the battle screen being clipped by the screen edge
- Fixed a bug that allowed to infinity sell weapons equipped by a character
- Fixed vanishing ammunition when the game was closed during the loading screen
- Fixed Mortar visuals when hit
- Added a new cursor
- Achievement fixes
- Audio fixes
- Visual fixes

78. The total number of titles that “the game currently known as WARSAW” tried on and dismissed before we decided to go with WARSAW itself. 
 
When we set out with an idea to create a game based on the Warsaw Rising we knew there was one major obstacle to overcome. Not a lot of people outside of Poland – and not everyone in the country for that matter – knows or knows intimately what Warsaw Rising was. 
 
This isn’t an accusation. Rather – stating the fact. And we don’t feel there is something wrong with it. We don’t come at anyone expecting them to know what Warsaw Rising was. Quite the opposite. The less you know – the better. Once you will play the game, that will change though. 
 
But not because we will drown you with facts, thrust down encyclopaedia worth of trivia down your throat and expose you to multitude of stats. But rather by sewing the fabric of the Warsaw Rising into the game mechanics themselves. Don’t know how long the Rising lasted? You will, as this is how long you need to make sure your characters live. Not sure what “błyskawica” is? You will by picking it up on one of the missions and equipping one of your heroes with it. Not sure where Długa is? You will, by traversing it during your patrols. Wonder what or who the Silent Unseen is? Ok, you get the point. 
 
Now. Making a game based on historical fact is one thing. Making sure anyone actually wants to play it is another. Main reason: not a lot of people care for the history of other countries. Not many care for their own. Lots of other things to do it turns out.
 
In order to interest people in the game about Warsaw Rising, we would have to not speak of the Warsaw Rising. At least not first. We wanted everyone to soak up the ambience. The visuals. The setting. The genre. And then, once we had the attention – there was no way to talk about the game without bringing up Warsaw Rising. At least as long as we had the right title. The one that would, without a doubt, indicate what the game was about. Easy. 

There was no guarantee that this would work, but it did. Well the exclusive reveal with GameSpot and the amazing trailer by Human Ark with Brodka’s moving rendition of Varsovie certainly did help. But... we’ll get to that part in a couple of days. 
 
Now back to the titles. We evaluated each of the candidates on a very subjective, 10 criteria scale. “Sequelability”, “Translationability”, "Freshness", “Memorability” were some of those. Our current title excelled in most of these. The only one where WARSAW actually underperformed is the one you can probably guess immediately. Yup. “Searchability”. 
 
You probably want to know what some of the other names we considered were. “[b]Heroes[/b]” (will get into that this Thursday), “[b]63[/b]” (spoiler) and “[b]Occupied[/b]” (uhh). 
 
To make sure no stone was left unturned we went after some famous musical numbers (“[b]No tears to cry[/b]”), movies (“[b]The edge of oppression[/b]”, “[b]Doomed Squad[/b]”), and everything "[b][b]Streets[/b][/b]":  (“(…) [b]of blood[/b]”, “(…) [b]of sorrow[/b]”, “(…) [b]of hope[/b]”, “(…) [b]of fire[/b]”, “(…) [b]of red[/b]”).  
 
The longest running champion was the “[b]Uncivil War[/b]”. At one point just a codename for the game it then morphed into a strongest candidate. “[b]Collateral City[/b]” also scored high. 
 
The search started on 12th of November, and almost to the day, two months later on 11th of January two victors emerged. [b]Uncivil War[/b] and [b]Warsaw[/b]. [b]Warsaw[/b] itself a result of taking the saw and pliers to Warsaw War and truncating it a little.  
 
Since we knew we wanted the game to be easily recognized both outside of Poland and in Poland, Uncivil war had to go. It just did not work in Polish. 
 
And so, [b]Warsaw[/b], and subsequently [b]WARSAW[/b] was born. Which was probably the last call as we felt we wanted to announce the game in February and wanted to go about it in the grandest way we could imagine. 

But let's not get ahead of ourselves, as this takes us into tomorrow’s tale about the inspirations behind how we wanted everyone to find out our super secret game no-one knew existed was coming out later this year...
